_doc: Daily chores (clarity pass, docs/CLARITY.md §2): what the household head asks of the player at dawn. Placeholders: {head} {player} {list} {strip} {side} {place} {label} {n} {kind} {church} {priest} {nb} {nbDesc} {title}.
say.done.2: {head}: 'Good. That is one less thing to worry about.'
strip.carry: Carry the sheaves from {strip} to the barn
strip.title.bind: Bind the sheaves on the {side} strip
strip.title.carry: Carry the sheaves from the {side} strip
strip.why.plough: {head} wants the ground turned while it is soft. A strip left fallow feeds nobody.
strip.why.harrow: The clods must be broken before the seed goes in, or the corn comes up thin.
strip.why.sow: The seed is in the barn and the season is short. Every day late costs a little of the harvest.
strip.why.weed: Unweeded corn yields a seventh less, and the family eats the difference.
strip.why.reap: The crop is ripe. Left standing it shatters in the field, and the tithe-man counts every sheaf.
strip.why.bind: The cut corn lies in the field: bind it into sheaves before the rain gets to it.
strip.why.carry: The sheaves stand in stooks. They keep best in the barn, and the pigs get at them in the field.
strip.hint: Stand on the strip and press E, or click it. Each press is a bout of work; the bar shows how far the task has come.
work.why.garden: The beds feed the pot between harvests: cabbages, onions and leeks do not weed themselves.
work.why.stock: The animals must be seen to every day: milk, hay and clean straw.
work.why.herd: The village beasts need driving out to the common pasture, and someone must mind them there.
work.why.craft: {head} needs the bench kept busy: finished work is coin, and your hands learn the trade.
work.why.barn: The sheaves are stacked in the barn. Until they are threshed and winnowed they are straw, not bread.
work.why.dig: Stone sells, and the quarry is open to any with a pick.
work.hint: Go to {place}, face it and press E (or click). Each press is a bout of work.
wood.title: Gather firewood
wood.why: The woodpile is low, and the nights are cold without a fire.
wood.why.plenty: A full woodpile is the best friend of a hard winter; fallen wood is free to anyone who gathers it.
wood.hint: Walk to the {kind} marked by the beacon and press E. Fallen wood needs no axe; the household's store grows when you stash it (I).
errand.title: Run an errand
errand.why: {nb} has a message and a basket to be carried, and a penny for whoever will carry them.
errand.hint: Walk up to {nb}, hold E for the action wheel and choose 'Run an errand'.
mass.title: Hear Mass
mass.why: It is the holy day: no work is done, and the whole parish goes to church. The priest notes who is missing.
mass.hint: Walk to the church and hold E: choose 'Hear Mass' (mornings of a holy day) or 'Pray'.
butts.title: Shoot at the butts
butts.why: On holy days the village men and boys shoot together, as the law requires. Practice is how an archer is made.
butts.hint: Hold E at the butts and choose 'Practise archery'. You need a bow and at least six arrows.
school.title: Lessons
school.why: A child who can read and reckon is worth more to the household than one who cannot.
school.hint: Talk to {priest}: ask a favour, and ask for lessons in letters.
week.title: Week-work on the lord's land
week.why: You owe the lord {days} this week; a day shirked is a fine, and the reeve keeps count.
week.hint: Stand on the lord's strip and press E. Every bout counts towards the week's dues.
job.why: {employer} expects you today. Your {title} pays by the day, and a master remembers who is idle.
job.do.hint: Face the workplace and press E, or click it. Each press is a bout of work.
job.report.hint: Find {employer} and press E to speak.
